source_text:
Προσέλθωμεν οὖν αὐτῷ ἐν ὁσιότητι ψυχῆς, ἁγνὰς καὶ ἀμιάντους χεῖρας αἴροντες πρὸς αὐτόν, ἀγαπῶντες τὸν ἐπιεικῆ καὶ εὔσπλαγχνον πατέρα ἡμῶν, ὃς ἐκλογῆς μέρος ἡμᾶς ἐποίησεν ἑαυτῷ.
οὕτω γὰρ γέγραπται: Ὅτε διεμέριζεν ὁ ὕψιστος ἔθνη, ὡς διέσπειρεν υἱοὺς Ἀδάμ, ἔστησεν ὅρια ἐθνῶν κατὰ ἀριθμὸν ἀγγέλων θεοῦ. ἐγενήθη μερὶς κυρίου λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰακώβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ τόπῳ λέγει: Ἰδού, κύριος λαμβάνει ἑαυτῷ ἔθνος ἐκ μέσου ἐθνῶν, ὥσπερ λαμβάνει ἄνθρωπος τὴν ἀπαρχὴν αὐτοῦ τῆς ἅλω: καὶ ἐξελεύσεται ἐκ τοῦ ἔθνους ἐκείνου ἅγια ἁγίων.
thought_title: Approach God in holiness as his chosen portion
orientation: The Roman church is exhorting the Corinthians to draw near to God in holiness, now grounding the call in Scripture about God choosing a people for himself.
pass_a_gloss: Let us approach him therefore in holiness of soul, lifting pure and undefiled hands toward him, loving the gentle and compassionate father of us, who made us a portion of choice for himself. For thus it is written: When the Most High divided nations, as he scattered sons of Adam, he set boundaries of nations according to number of angels of God. The portion of the Lord became his people Jacob, the measured line of his inheritance Israel. And in another place he says: Behold, the Lord takes for himself a nation from the midst of nations, just as a man takes his firstfruits from the threshing floor: and there shall come out from that nation holy things of holies.

choices.why: Keeps the genitive force of ἐκλογῆς as a defining quality of the portion, matching the scriptural language of Israel as God's chosen portion; avoids the smoother 'chosen portion' to preserve the noun 'choice' visible in the source.

choices.english: the measured line of his inheritance
choices.why: σχοίνισμα is a measuring cord or allotment line; rendering it as 'measured line' keeps the concrete image of land measured out for inheritance, which 'portion' would blur.

This is a literal rendering of the Hebrew superlative construction; it preserves the source's exact phrase rather than normalizing to 'the holy of holies' or 'most holy things,' keeping the oddness of the Greek.
Keeps the dative phrase as a state or sphere in which the approach happens, and retains 'soul' as the locus of holiness rather than collapsing it into an adjective.

bible_refs.note: Ὅτε διεμέριζεν ὁ ὕψιστος ἔθνη, ὡς διέσπειρεν υἱοὺς Ἀδάμ, ἔστησεν ὅρια ἐθνῶν κατὰ ἀριθμὸν ἀγγέλων θεοῦ. ἐγενήθη μερὶς κυρίου λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰακώβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
Ἰδού, κύριος λαμβάνει ἑαυτῷ ἔθνος ἐκ μέσου ἐθνῶν, ὥσπερ λαμβάνει ἄνθρωπος τὴν ἀπαρχὴν αὐτοῦ τῆς ἅλω: καὶ ἐξελεύσεται ἐκ τοῦ ἔθνους ἐκείνου ἅγια ἁγίων.

pass_b_english: Let us approach him, then, in holiness of soul, lifting pure and undefiled hands toward him, and loving our gentle and compassionate Father, who made us a portion of choice for himself.

For it is written this way: When the Most High was dividing the nations, when he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of God's angels. The Lord's portion became his people Jacob; Israel became the measured line of his inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:8-9).

And in another place he says: Look, the Lord takes for himself a nation from the midst of nations, just as a person takes his firstfruits from the threshing floor; and from that nation will come forth holy things of holies.

problems.why: Deut 4:34 is unrelated; this quotes Deut 33:3 LXX, 'holy ones of holies'.
problems.ruling: source phrase ἅγια ἁγίων not found in Deut 4:34; it occurs in Deut 33:3 LXX, so citation is incorrect

problems.quote: from that nation will come forth holy things of holies
problems.why: Cited as Deuteronomy 33:3, but this phrase does not appear in standard texts of that verse.
problems.fix: Note this is a loose paraphrase or follows a variant LXX reading.

variants.text: from that nation will come forth holy things of holies

edits.old: and from that nation will come forth holy things of holies (Deuteronomy 33:3).
edits.new: and from that nation will come forth holy things of holies.

fixed: Removed the incorrect Scripture citation (Deuteronomy 33:3) from the phrase 'holy things of holies', since the phrase does not appear in standard texts of that verse and the source does not specify a citation.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by making the sequence of actions explicit and adding 'and' before 'loving' so the reader can follow the flow of worship, while keeping every claim and Scripture reference intact.

last_rejected.why: The quote is from Deuteronomy 33:3 LXX, but 'holy things of holies' is a mistranslation; it refers to holy of holies or holy ones.
last_rejected.fix: holy ones of the holy ones (Deuteronomy 33:3)
last_rejected.ruling: Greek ἅγια ἁγίων means 'holy things of the holy'; translation 'holy things of holies' is literal, albeit awkward, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: who made us a portion of choice for himself
last_rejected.source_quote: ὃς ἐκλογῆς μέρος ἡμᾶς ἐποίησεν ἑαυτῷ.
last_rejected.why: ‘ἐκλογῆς’ is rendered as ‘choice’, but glossary requires ‘the elect’.
last_rejected.fix: who made us a portion of the elect for himself
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκλογῆς can mean 'choice' or 'election'; 'portion of choice' conveys the genitive adequately without misleading the reader.
